transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-09 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Morgan, Priya Shah (Redwood); Dr. Marcus Lee, Sofia Ramirez, Evan Cole, Lina Park (Veridian)

Summary: quick review of last week's quality evals, prompt tuning notes, and next steps for regression checks and guardrails. Discussion of a couple of low-confidence areas in the prompt sets (disambiguation on medication names, hallucination in diagnosis text).

Topics: quality metrics, prompt sets v1.2 -> v1.3, scoring rubric thresholds, false-positive guardrails, security/infra notes, next steps and action items.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll try to keep this to 45 minutes. Quick roll call, and then Priya will walk through the latest quality numbers.
[00:10] Dr. Marcus Lee: Hey Alex, hey Priya. Marcus here. We've got Lina and Evan with me.
[00:14] Sofia Ramirez: Sofia as well.
[00:16] Priya Shah: Great. Ok, so this week we ran the v1.2 prompt bank across the 3 eval sets you shared — clinical triage, escalation, and triage edge cases. Overall accuracy by our surrogate label match is up slightly, 72% -> 76% on the triage set. But we did see a regression on hallucination score for medication extraction.
[00:33] Lina Park: Yeah the medication bit is concerning, we caught a few cases where the model invents dosages.
[00:38] Priya Shah: Right, we saw several where the prompt didn't implicitly require numeric validation so the model confidently filled in numbers. We're proposing a guardrail to call out: 'If dosage not explicit, respond "unspecified" and ask for clarification'. That's in v1.3.
[00:52] Evan Cole: Quick infra question — when you say regression, is that on hosted or the dedicated staging cluster? We've been testing on a local fork and also hitting Dedicated staging. Latency there is a little worse than production expectations.
[01:05] Priya Shah: Good question. The numbers in the spreadsheet are from the Hosted run. We also ran a small Dedicated staging pass — latency avg was 160ms per token for the long-form path, likely due to packing policy. We'll schedule a more controlled Dedicated benchmark next week with consistent sequence lengths.
[01:23] Alex Morgan: To add, the KV cache behaviour in staging can vary if the prefix caching isn't warmed. Evan, when you send logs, Priya can correlate cache misses to the higher p95.
[01:33] Evan Cole: Will do. I'll pull a sample of logs showing the cache misses and the sequence lengths.
[01:38] Dr. Marcus Lee: Back to quality: the scoring rubric — can we quickly recap the thresholds you used? I remember we had the precision threshold at 0.85 for critical entities, is that still set?
[01:48] Priya Shah: Yes, critical-entity precision is set to 0.85 for pass. For acceptability we used F1>0.7. We added a new hallucination metric that measures unsupported medical facts; we flagged anything above 0.2 hallucination rate as a fail. Several medication extraction cases pushed that over for v1.2.
[02:05] Sofia Ramirez: How are you detecting hallucinations? Is it rule-based or model-based?
[02:09] Priya Shah: It's a hybrid. We run a deterministic name/number extractor then a secondary check using a smaller retrieval model to see if the claimed fact matches the records in the reference set. The retrieval sometimes misses obscure meds, which leads to false positives. We're tuning the retrieval threshold.
[02:23] Lina Park: That makes sense. We can also provide an external drug list to reduce false negatives.
[02:27] Dr. Marcus Lee: Good, please do.
[02:30] Alex Morgan: Ok, on guardrails — beyond the dosage behavior, we want to add explicit instruction templates for uncertain outputs: e.g., 'If uncertain, say you are not sure and ask follow-up question + include confidence score.' This tends to reduce hallucinated completions.
[02:44] Priya Shah: We've drafted that in v1.3. Also added a 'structured answer' requirement for any diagnosis response so downstream systems can validate fields.
[02:52] Evan Cole: One other topic — encryption/KMS. Our security review flagged a question about token-level logging: do you redact PII by default in logs?
[03:00] Alex Morgan: Short answer — yes, we have PII redaction pipeline for logs; we can provide the SOC2 section and the redaction pattern docs. I'll send links after the call.
[03:08] Sofia Ramirez: Please include SSO/SAML setup notes — we'll need them for the pilot.
[03:12] Alex Morgan: Yup, adding that to action items.
[03:14] Priya Shah: Back to the results: we also ran the prompt variations A and B. Variation A improved recall on escalation intent (from 68% to 77%) but lowered precision on non-urgent triage calls. There's a tradeoff; suggestion is to use A for high-sensitivity routing and B for production default. We recommend a canary rollout with traffic split 10/90 to measure real-world impact.
[03:36] Dr. Marcus Lee: That fits our risk posture — we prefer conservative defaults. Can we add automatic fallback to a simpler rules engine if the model confidence < 0.6?
[03:45] Priya Shah: Absolutely, that fallback rule is quick to implement in the routing layer. We'll include that in the canary config.
[03:51] Evan Cole: For Dedicated/Private deployment planning — do you see any blockers for us moving the pilot to Dedicated later this month?
[03:58] Alex Morgan: No blockers from Redwood side; just need VPC creds for connectivity tests and to validate KMS integration. We recommend a brief network dry-run.
[04:07] Lina Park: We'll coordinate with Evan on the creds.
[04:09] Sofia Ramirez: A user question — on the UI side, can we surface confidence and a short provenance note for each recommended action?
[04:16] Priya Shah: Yes, we can output confidence and a provenance token (e.g., 'retrieved-from: clinical_notes_v2,score:0.73') but provenance strings might leak internal ids; we'll normalize them.
[04:27] Dr. Marcus Lee: Also -- slightly tangential but we saw some bad behavior on short prompts where the model repeats the question back. Might be a beam/decoding artifact. Any quick fixes?
[04:36] Priya Shah: Usually decoding temperature and repetition penalty handle that. We'll try a slightly lower temperature and a higher repetition penalty in v1.3 test.
[04:44] Alex Morgan: Ok let's recap action items and next steps. Priya will share prompt v1.3 with the dosage guardrail and structured outputs. Alex will send SOC2 and redaction docs and SSO setup. Evan will provide VPC creds and logs. Marcus will flag the top clinical failures. We'll meet next Wednesday for the regression check.
[04:59] Dr. Marcus Lee: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:02] Alex Morgan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

Notes/Links referenced: prompt-v1.3-draft (link: https://redwood.company/prompt-v1-3), quality-spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.company/qa/spreadsheet-88732), SOC2-summary (link: https://redwood.company/security/soc2), redaction-patterns doc (link: https://redwood.company/security/redaction).

End of transcript.
